what: The score is insertion cost minus the candidate's standalone depot round-trip cost. Thus lower scores maximize the distance saving obtained by absorbing the customer into the current route rather than leaving it as a potential future route seed. It uses the caller-fixed insertion position and costs O(1) time and memory.
why: Plain cheapest insertion can favor customers with small absolute detours even when they are near the depot, leaving distant customers to incur expensive depot legs later. The proposed score is the negative of a Clarke–Wright-style insertion saving: 2*d(depot, customer) minus the fixed-position insertion cost. It therefore rewards both geometric compatibility with the current route and avoidance of costly future depot travel. The coefficient has a direct interpretation rather than being instance-scale dependent. This remains a greedy construction score, not a remaining-cost estimate: it does not model competing future insertions, capacity fragmentation, RCL randomness, or the exact changes made by subsequent 2-opt, so it should be validated on held-out families.
